protocol: D-000; independent adversarial review; refute not confirm; successor to CONTESTED D-031/D-024
summary: The §3.1 defect that contested D-031 is genuinely fixed: there is now exactly one instruction — the instrument starts, on Lane R — and no closing-list prohibition contradicts it. The D-025 dependency is gone and the scheduling rule is stated in full. The five-step rationale is not circular; its steps chain 1 to 2 to 3 to 4 to 5 with no cycle, and I verified its load-bearing empirical claim: DR-105 and DR-114 are both still OPEN in the register at its current digest, so 'the actor defect already blocks two OPEN rows' holds even after D-035. Two MUST-FIX defects remain. The entry carries no digests at all — no measured-inputs table, no re-measurement clause, nothing — and it makes unpinned factual claims about two documents that have both moved since the predecessor cycle. And the preemption rule, which the entry names as its own principal gain, keys on an undefined term: 'owner' is never defined, the coordinator drafts on both lanes, and on either available reading the rule is unexecutable as a parallelism guarantee.

objections.claim: The draft contains no digests of any kind — no measured-inputs table, no re-measurement clause, no pin on any cited source — while making factual claims about two documents that have both moved since the predecessor cycle it supersedes.
objections.evidence: Measured: the draft contains zero substrings of 16 or more hexadecimal characters, and zero occurrences of 'Measured inputs', 're-measured', or 'moved source'. Every prior draft in this lineage carried a four-row measured-inputs table plus the clause 'If a cited file moves before adoption, the citing sentence is re-measured. A moved source is not silently treated as the same source', and the D-025-031 turn-2 and turn-3 drafts additionally carried the property-pin scoping naming which sections of COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md the whole-document pin supports. All of it is gone. The omission is not theoretical: measured at review time, file 08 has moved from a3e37102991b80502aa1f9fb1affe2011859917b8ce1477a93f494485b9161b7 to 5e1a75a542c3a4914d44a5093a057d89a39e140b84011a85d56ed0d769c19f07, and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md from a563510d96ddad8b3d4c9e2adb80216d94d21b33a0b9fc6350586631d1ba4405 to 9d41c5ba217716869b22c3c5c6e1036b55141e7370c5ad1ac07fc79f3bb663d5, via commits d572122 (D-035) and fcb1198. The draft rests substantive claims on both: that the actor defect 'already blocks two OPEN rows' (a file-08 row-status claim), that 'D-001 already commissioned' the §3.1 instrument (a COORDINATOR-DECISIONS claim), and that D-028, D-029 and D-030 are ADOPTED (also COORDINATOR-DECISIONS). I verified all three independently and all three are true — but the entry provides no means for a later reader to reproduce that, which is the whole function of the pin discipline. This is the corpus's central control, the subject of freeze §7.10 and of DR-204's anchoring adjudication, and it is the axis this review prompt names last.
objections.proposedFix: Restore the measured-inputs table with file 08 at 5e1a75a5…, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 9d41c5ba…, and the join review at 538f3681…; restore the re-measurement clause verbatim; and restore the property-pin scoping naming the sections actually used, which for this entry are D-001's DR-004 route-A line commissioning the §3.1 instrument, D-001 SF-3, and the D-028/D-029/D-030 adoption records.

objections.claim: The preemption rule is not executable. 'Owner' is nowhere defined, the coordinator is the drafter on both lanes, and on either available reading the rule fails — one collapses the two lanes into serialization and silently reinstates the deprioritization the entry's own Alternatives section rejects; the other leaves the rule almost never binding.
objections.evidence: The rule reads: 'When Lane R and Lane P contend for the same owner, Lane R goes first; Lane P waits on that owner, not the reverse.' The term 'owner' appears nowhere else in the draft and is not defined. Two readings are available and the draft does not choose. Reading one, 'owner' includes the coordinator: then the rule binds continuously, because Lane R is defined as 'all outstanding authoritative-path work under file 08 and D-001' with a non-exhaustive list spanning DR-002 through DR-008 plus the §3.1 instrument, and the coordinator is the actor for Lane P steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 and the drafter for step 4. Lane R will not be empty for the foreseeable corpus, so Lane P never proceeds — which is exactly the outcome the Alternatives section rejects as 'Sequence Route A after preview. Rejected: deprioritization', and which contradicts the entry's stated gain that the lanes run together. Reading two, 'owner' means only the V1 surface authorities named by file 08 — Evidence authority, Threat-model authority, evidence/retention authority, and so on — which is what the Honesty section's phrase 'preview work yields to V1 owners' suggests: then the rule almost never binds, because Lane P work is coordinator work and those authorities do not execute it. The adopted D-028, D-029 and D-030 already fix the division of labour that creates this ambiguity — 'the coordinator may draft; the owning V1 authority records' — so the coordinator is simultaneously a Lane P actor and a Lane R drafter by adopted rule, and the entry does not say whether that counts as contention. The entry's Honesty section claims 'a defined preemption rule' as one of its two gains; on this text it is not defined.
objections.proposedFix: Define 'owner' explicitly, and state whether coordinator drafting capacity is in scope. If it is, scope the preemption per work item rather than lane-wide — for example, Lane R preempts Lane P only for the specific row whose owner both lanes need — so Lane P is not permanently blocked by a lane that is non-empty by construction. If it is not, say so, and state what governs coordinator capacity instead, since that is the actual contended resource.

objections.claim: The draft omits the decision type, which D-000's entry format lists as a required field and which determines whether clause 5's preference-laden treatment applies.
objections.evidence: Measured: 'decision type' occurs zero times in the draft. D-000's entry format, at COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, requires: 'id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives considered, rationale, reviewer + verdict + digest, DECISION TYPE (MECHANICAL | RULE-GOVERNED | PREFERENCE-LADEN), reversibility, overturn procedure, commit.' Checked against that list, D-036 supplies id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives, rationale (its 'Why this order' and 'Honesty' sections), reversibility and overturn procedure; reviewer verdict and commit land at adoption; decision type is the sole required field absent. The omission is consequential rather than cosmetic: an execution-sequence entry choosing an order and a preemption rule is preference-laden — both of its predecessors, D-024 and D-031, were marked PREFERENCE-LADEN — and D-000 clause 5 requires such entries be marked and their overturn procedure written to cost less than the decision did. Without the marking, the clause-5 obligation is unstated.
objections.proposedFix: Add 'Decision type: PREFERENCE-LADEN' to the header block, matching D-024 and D-031.

objections.claim: The no-blueprint caveat present in the predecessor is dropped, so nothing in this entry states that it does not authorize implementation.
objections.evidence: CONTESTED D-031's corresponding clause read: 'File 08 is already the only live readiness plan. Execute it until D-001's five conditions hold and condition 5 authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.' D-036's replacement reads: 'File 08 remains the only readiness plan. Condition 2/4 follow D-001 SF-3.' The condition-5 sentence is gone, and this draft carries no closing 'What these entries do not do' list, which in the predecessor drafts opened with 'Do not authorize docs/v2/implementation/'. No misreading is likely — the scheduling rule confines the entry to authorizing drafting, and Lane R is V1 successor work rather than implementation — so this is disclosure hygiene rather than a live risk. I record it because the entry newly contains an affirmative start instruction ('This entry starts Lane R: the coordinator begins or continues that work on adoption') over a non-exhaustive set, which is the first time in this lineage a sequence entry has started anything, and that is the context in which the missing caveat is worth restoring.
objections.proposedFix: Restore the condition-5 sentence, or add one line stating that this entry authorizes no blueprint and that condition 5 remains the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: ac2a827dca0f6d89b289260e2fe1213bdea3e2b8cafed5c9e70c2e9b3fa4b5c3 both times. No drift.

The §3.1 single-instruction question, which is the defect that contested D-031: RESOLVED. Lane R states 'the freeze §3.1 item-to-supplier binding instrument (D-001 already commissioned this; this entry starts its authoring on Lane R; it is not a file-11 item)'. There is no closing-list prohibition anywhere in the draft, so no competing instruction exists. The Alternatives section additionally names and rejects both wrong answers — treating it as a file-11 item, and not starting it — with the second rejection citing the turn-3 contradiction by name.

The §3.1 attribution is accurate. D-001's DR-004 route-A line reads 'route A: the exact eight-bullet Phase-1A packet; plus commission the missing §3.1-item-to-supplier binding instrument.' The draft's claim that D-001 already commissioned it, and its placement on Route A rather than as a file-11 item, are both exact.

The five-step rationale is not circular. The dependency chain is 1 (product decisions change which rows are slice-affecting) to 2 (pin/history mechanics make later closures survivable) to 3 (the actor defect blocks two OPEN rows) to 4 (dispositions require those product and actor facts, so 4 depends on 1 and 3) to 5 (analyze needs the dispositions' scope, so 5 depends on 4). No step depends on a later step and no cycle exists.

The rationale's load-bearing empirical claim holds at current bytes, which I checked because file 08 has moved and D-035 touched DR-114. Measured in file 08 at 5e1a75a5: DR-105 is 'OPEN — candidate authored 2026-08-13, independent review DISPATCHED and not yet returned'; DR-114 is 'OPEN — design contract ACCEPTED 2026-08-13 (D-035); the actor-join and fixture-execution halves remain open.' Both rows are OPEN and the actor-join half specifically remains open, so 'the actor defect already blocks two OPEN rows' is true post-D-035.

The D-025 dependency is gone. The header states 'D-025 is not required; this entry states its own scheduling rule in full', and the body delivers it: 'Scheduling rule (self-contained). Inclusion here authorizes drafting only. Live work still requires D-001 Route A, B, or C.' No clause cites D-025. This is material because D-025 was never adopted — verified below — so a dependency on it would have been a dependency on nothing.

Adoption states asserted by the header are accurate, verified against the register rather than the draft. COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 9d41c5ba contains D-028 'ADOPTED 2026-08-13', D-029 'ADOPTED 2026-08-13' and D-030 'ADOPTED 2026-08-13'. D-025, D-026, D-027 and D-031 have no entries at all, so the header's silence on D-025 through D-027 and its treatment of D-031 as CONTESTED are both correct. Lane P step 4's scoping to 'adopted selectors (D-028, D-029, D-030, and any later adopted siblings)' matches that state exactly, and correctly excludes DR-002 and DR-004, whose selectors were not adopted and which appear on Lane R in full.

No silent D-001 amendment. 'File 08 remains the only readiness plan. Condition 2/4 follow D-001 SF-3' cites SF-3 without constraining it. 'Estimates do not change D-001 done; they are not a gate' is consistent with D-001's five-condition definition. 'Live work still requires D-001 Route A, B, or C' restates the route set without adding or closing one.

Supersession scope: 'CONTESTED D-031 / D-024 only' is coherent. D-024 belongs to the terminated D-017-D-024 cycle and D-031 to the CONTESTED D-025-D-031 cycle; neither was adopted, and superseding an unadopted contested draft is the same construction the adopted D-028, D-029 and D-030 used.
The protocol line reads 'D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3', which is correct for this dispatch — the stale-turn-label defect I raised against the D-025-031 turn-3 draft has not recurred.
Reversibility carries a temporal boundary: 'Total before execution. After dependents land, supersession is prospective. Overturn: C-D036 only.'
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex verdict on D-036. Not read.

Codex's MUST-FIX text against D-031, which the draft header characterizes as 'incompatible start / do-not-start for the §3.1 instrument'. I never read that verdict; I verified the repair against the bytes and against my own turn-3 finding C2N3-D031-01, which described the same contradiction.
Whether the chosen five-step order is the best order. Preference-laden and inside the coordinator's D-000 authority; I checked only for circularity, executability, and conflict with adopted bytes.
Whether Lane R's non-exhaustive list is complete. Non-exhaustive by construction; I verified it names DR-002 through DR-008 and the §3.1 instrument and did not hunt for an omitted obligation.
The DR-105/DR-114 actor defect on its merits, beyond confirming both rows are OPEN and that the actor-join half of DR-114 remains open after D-035.
D-032 through D-035 as entries. D-035 is adopted and I read only its effect on DR-114's status; D-032 is the subject of a separate review in this session and is not assessed here.

convergenceNote: The defect that contested D-031 is fixed, and fixed cleanly — one instruction, correctly attributed, with both wrong answers named and rejected. Neither MUST-FIX contests a decision this entry makes: the two lanes, the order, the §3.1 start, and the preemption direction all survive attack. C2-D036-01 asks for a table this lineage carried six times and this draft dropped; C2-D036-03 asks for one header field. Only C2-D036-02 requires the coordinator to decide something new — what 'owner' means and whether coordinator capacity is in scope — and that question is forced by adopted bytes, since D-028, D-029 and D-030 already make the coordinator the drafter on both lanes.
